Drug properties affecting response: 2

A large therapeutic protein has poor passive intestinal membrane absorption compared with many small molecules. Which physical characteristic helps explain why simply placing it in an ordinary oral tablet may not provide reliable systemic exposure?

  1. Lipid solubility and membrane passage
  2. Formulation-dependent release
  3. Additive pharmacodynamic effects
  4. Complex formation reducing absorption
  5. Molecular size limiting passive membrane passage
Answer and explanation

Molecular size limiting passive membrane passage

Large molecules often cross lipid membranes poorly without specialized transport or delivery.

Option explanations

Molecular size limiting passive membrane passage: Large molecules often cross lipid membranes poorly without specialized transport or delivery.

Lipid solubility and membrane passage: Physicochemical properties influence membrane penetration, distribution and sometimes CNS entry. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Formulation-dependent release: Immediate- and modified-release products can have different concentration-time profiles despite containing the same drug. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Additive pharmacodynamic effects: Two medicines with similar physiological actions can increase the combined effect or toxicity. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Complex formation reducing absorption: Binding of some medicines to polyvalent cations can reduce gastrointestinal absorption. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
